sections.h2: Which Jackson County office sends the tax bill?
sections.html:
In Jackson County the bill is the Tax Collector's job, and the office runs an online portal that pulls up a parcel's bill by tax year. The Property Appraiser supplies the values. Rates are set by the County Commission, the School Board and other districts.

On jacksontc.com, a page called "Due Dates and Discounts" runs through the year month by month. Vehicle and license deadlines share that page with property tax, so the rows below pull out the property ones. Lay them beside your contract date to see which deadline comes next.

Jackson County keeps Central Time, so check the clock before an online payment on a month's last day.

sections.h2: What are the Jackson County property tax months?
sections.html:
Collection opens in November and closes at the gross amount on March 31, with the discount shrinking between.

Property tax rows from the Jackson County Tax Collector Due Dates and Discounts page (jacksontc.com)
MonthCalendar entry
NovemberCollection opens; 4% discount if paid by November 30
December3% discount
January2% discount
February1% discount
MarchGross amount due by March 31
AprilUnpaid real property tax delinquent on April 1; 3% penalty

Business equipment (tangible personal property) follows the same discount months. That row rarely matters to a homeowner, but a landlord or a seller who ran a business from the property should read it.

sections.h2: What does the Jackson County calendar say about delinquent accounts?
sections.html:
Real property tax left unpaid on April 1 picks up a 3% penalty. The calendar says the delinquent list goes into a local newspaper inside 45 days, at the owner's expense, then repeats weekly for three weeks in May before the certificate sale. Since the sale date is chosen in March, a seller can learn it before delinquency even begins.

An investor who buys a certificate holds a lien, not the house. After two years pass without redemption, the investor may apply for a deed and the clerk holds an auction. For a homestead parcel, statute 197.502 puts half of the latest assessed value into the opening bid, on top of what is owed.

Equipment taxes run on a different clock: 1.5% interest a month, advertising inside 45 days, and tax warrant work from May 1.

sections.h2: Can Jackson County owners spread payments over the year?
sections.html:
Yes. The collector's calendar describes a plan of four payments toward the next year's tax, with applications due April 30. Enrolled owners stay in without reapplying.

  • First payment: due on or before June 1, with cancellation if nothing arrives by June 30.
  • Second payment: before September 30.
  • Third payment: by December 31.
  • Final payment: by March 31.

The first item gives two different dates, so call the office and confirm which applies to your account. If you sell while on the plan, give the closing agent a list of paid installments so the proration is right.

sections.h2: Which homestead and assessment limits matter to a Jackson County seller?
sections.html:
Homestead in Jackson County works as it does statewide: live in the house on January 1, file DR-501 by March 1, and up to $50,000 comes off assessed value. Only the first $25,000 lowers school tax.

Growth in a homestead's assessed value is held to the lesser of 3 percent or inflation, and the state's chart lists 2.7 percent for 2026. Non-homestead parcels face a 10 percent cap. Selling ends both, so a buyer's first bill often exceeds the seller's last.

  • Seniors: a county or city ordinance may add an exemption for owners 65 or older within an income limit.
  • Veterans: a service-connected disability of 10 percent or more can bring a $5,000 reduction in assessed value.
  • Leasing the house or leaving it removes homestead status.

Ask the Property Appraiser whether a local ordinance applies to your address.

sections.h2: What is the route for contesting a Jackson County value?
sections.html:
TRIM notices are mailed in August, and a Value Adjustment Board petition must follow within 25 days. For a denied exemption, 30 days run from the denial letter.

Talk to the appraiser's staff first. A wrong square footage figure or exemption status may be fixed without a hearing, and a deed, survey or builder's records help if the record itself is wrong.

sections.h2: Does the November 2026 property tax amendment affect a Jackson County bill?
sections.html:
The county announced a town hall on October 13, 2026 about Amendment 3, a property tax proposal on the November 2026 ballot. The notice said the discussion would cover the possible effect on local funding for public safety, fire and emergency services and special districts. It describes the amendment as proposed, so no figures appear.

The October 13 meeting started at 6:00 p.m. Central Time at the Endeavor Convention Center, was free to attend, and invited local governments, law enforcement, fire and emergency medical services and special taxing districts to take part. That guest list shows who relies on property tax revenue in the county, and who may adjust budgets if the rules change.

What changes depends on the ballot result and any law that follows. Check the Florida Department of Revenue and county budget pages for the effective year before relying on a number in a sale. Until new rules are posted, use the dates and amounts on your own bill.

sections.h2: Do mobile homes and business equipment follow the same dates in Jackson County?
sections.html:
Partly. The collector's calendar treats tangible personal property, such as business furniture and equipment, on the same discount schedule as real estate, but with the harsher 1.5% monthly interest charge once it turns delinquent.

Mobile homes have their own line. A mobile home that is not assessed as real property needs its decal renewed by December 31, and the calendar puts registration of mobile homes, trucks over 8,000 pounds and truck-trailers in the same December window. If you own a mobile home on land you are selling, ask the tax collector whether it is billed as real property or carries a decal, since that decides which deadline you face.

Both points are worth raising with the closing agent early. Tell them whether the property includes a mobile home or business equipment, so that every account tied to it is identified and paid before the settlement date.

sections.h2: What should a Jackson County seller line up before closing?
sections.html:
Get the payoff in writing, with the tax year it covers. The title agent then divides the current year between buyer and seller at the closing table.

  • Use the portal's tax-year search to check whether earlier years remain open.
  • If April 1 has passed, ask about the penalty and advertising costs.
  • Look for recorded liens in the Clerk's records.
  • Hand the closing agent your installment history.

A seller racing a delinquency or certificate sale date can set a quick cash closing, with the tax paid out of proceeds by the title agent.

faqs.q: What is the final day to pay Jackson County property tax without a penalty?
faqs.a: March 31 is the cutoff for the gross amount. Paying early earns 4% in November, then 3%, 2% and 1% in the following three months.

faqs.q: What penalty hits an unpaid Jackson County bill on April 1?
faqs.a: Real property takes a 3% penalty. Business equipment is charged 1.5% interest a month instead.

faqs.q: When does Jackson County hold its tax certificate sale?
faqs.a: The collector fixes the date in March, ahead of the April 1 delinquency date. The collector's announcements give the exact day.

faqs.q: Does Jackson County allow installment payments?
faqs.a: Yes. File by April 30 for next year's plan and pay in June, September, December and March. Ask the office for the exact June date.

faqs.q: Will selling raise the next owner's Jackson County bill?
faqs.a: Usually, yes. The Save Our Homes cap and the 10 percent limit both end at a sale, and the next January 1 resets the property to just value.
